topic: PM launches nationwide dengue prevention campaign
headline_marked: [[PM launches 3-month nationwide dengue prevention and cleanliness campaign]]
headline: PM launches 3-month nationwide dengue prevention and cleanliness campaign
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated a three-month nationwide campaign to combat dengue and promote cleanliness, urging public cooperation for a healthier Bangladesh.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman officially launched a three-month nationwide dengue prevention and cleanliness campaign on Saturday morning. The inauguration took place at the South Plaza of the Parliament House.

During the event, the Prime Minister called for the cooperation of all citizens across the country to effectively prevent dengue and maintain a clean environment. He stressed that collective effort is crucial for national transformation.

The campaign is scheduled to run from September 12 to December 12, aiming to make maximum efforts to tackle the dengue problem. While a 100% solution might not be possible, effective initiatives will be taken to control the situation.

Prime Minister Rahman urged everyone to dedicate one hour each week to cleanliness, stating that this commitment would bring about a significant change in the situation. He emphasized the importance of keeping oneself and society healthy.

He also appealed to citizens to refrain from littering indiscriminately, highlighting that every individual has a role in building a clean nation. He referenced the public's demonstration on August 5, 2024, as proof that change is possible, now urging for a transformation of the state.
Before the official inauguration, the Prime Minister visited various stalls set up at the event and interacted with common people, shaking hands with them.
caption:

The campaign is scheduled to run from September 12 to December 12, aiming to make maximum efforts to tackle the dengue problem. While a 100% solution might not be possible, effective initiatives will be taken to control the situation.

Prime Minister Rahman urged everyone to dedicate one hour each week to cleanliness, stating that this commitment would bring about a significant change in the situation. He emphasized the importance of keeping oneself and society healthy.

He also appealed to citizens to refrain from littering indiscriminately, highlighting that every individual has a role in building a clean nation. He referenced the public's demonstration on August 5, 2024, as proof that change is possible, now urging for a transformation of the state.

topic: Chhatra Dal leader missing in Padma River
headline_marked: Bulkhead collision: [[Chhatra Dal leader missing]] after falling into Padma River
headline: Bulkhead collision: Chhatra Dal leader missing after falling into Padma River
summary: Rakibuzzaman Rocky, member secretary of Shailkupa Pourashava Chhatra Dal, went missing after a boat trip collision near the Hardinge Bridge.
details: A Chhatra Dal leader, Rakibuzzaman Rocky (32), has gone missing after falling into the Padma River in Bheramara, Kushtia, following a bulkhead collision with a bridge pillar.

The accident occurred around 9 PM on Friday night. A group of 123 people from the Katlagari area of Shailkupa, Jhenaidah, were on a boat trip when the vessel lost control due to strong currents and hit the 4th pillar of the Hardinge Bridge.
Three people fell into the river during the impact. Two passengers, identified as Liton and Ohab, were immediately rescued by other passengers and are reported to be safe.

Rakibuzzaman Rocky, the member secretary of Shailkupa Pourashava Chhatra Dal, remains missing. Rescue operations were launched by members of the Ishwardi and Bheramara Fire Service, along with Naval Police.
The Bheramara Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) and the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Bheramara Police Station confirmed that multiple units are continuing search efforts to locate the missing leader.
